mcat_description.short: GRP (Glass Reinforced Plastic) cabins are prefabricated portable enclosures moulded from fibreglass-reinforced polyester resin panels, sold as complete ready-to-install units or in knock-down panel form for on-site assembly.
mcat_description.long: GRP cabins are prefabricated structures constructed from moulded glass-reinforced plastic panels — a composite of thermosetting polyester or vinylester resin reinforced with chopped strand mat (CSM) or woven glass fibres — offering high strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance, and weatherproofing. In the Indian market they are manufactured and supplied primarily as security guard cabins, portable site offices, toilet blocks, bunkhouses, and telecom/equipment shelters, with panel thickness typically 6–10 mm and polyurethane foam or glass wool insulation injected between skins. Cabins are customisable in size (commonly 4×4 ft to 20×10 ft), colour via gel coat finish, and fittings (aluminium sliding windows, PVC or MS doors, electrical wiring, plumbing). The material is non-conductive, virtually maintenance-free, fire-retardant when treated, and fully relocatable, making it a preferred alternative to MS or sandwich-panel portable cabins in corrosive or coastal environments.

market_context: GRP cabins are known interchangeably as FRP cabins in the Indian market — GRP is the British/European term while FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic) is the American and widely adopted Indian trade term for the same composite material. The material is a thermosetting plastic (most often polyester or vinylester resin) reinforced with glass fibres in chopped strand mat (CSM) or woven fabric form. Indian manufacturers are concentrated in Mumbai, Pune, Pimpri Chinchwad, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, and Ghaziabad. The dominant commercial products in India are security guard cabins (4×4 ft to 6×6 ft) and portable site offices (up to 20×10 ft), with panel wall thickness typically 7 mm and polyurethane foam or glass wool insulation as standard. Key differentiators buyers compare include cabin size, wall/panel thickness, insulation type, fire retardancy, gel coat colour, and included fittings (windows, doors, electrical). GRP/FRP cabins compete directly with MS (mild steel) portable cabins and sandwich panel cabins — GRP is preferred in coastal, corrosive, or high-humidity environments due to its non-rusting, non-conductive properties. No mandatory BIS/IS standard governs GRP cabins specifically in India (single source — low confidence); quality is typically self-certified by manufacturers. Buyers include construction contractors, industrial facility managers, telecom companies, government bodies, and resort developers.
